fichas.title: Bowling Alleys: Areas, Layout, and Equipment
fichas.summary: A bowling alley is organized into a run-up area, the ball-rolling lane, and a catching area for pins and balls. The page illustrates lane constructions, pin arrangements, side channels, alley layouts, and a double bowling lane. Run-up areas use cleanly sanded parquet; lanes are polished or varnished parquet. Balls and pins are made from standardized materials and sizes.
uses: Roll the ball after a few steps
Roll the ball along the lane
Collect standing or fallen pins and the bowling ball

fichas.title: Asphalt Bowling Track
fichas.summary: The asphalt track is described as a specialized sporting track with demanding surfacing. The lane may be asphalt or plastic and is shown with side bands or side channels. The diagrams also show pin arrangements and possible side-channel constructions.
uses: Roll balls on a specialized asphalt or plastic track

fichas.title: Planked Bowling Lane
fichas.summary: The planked lane originated as a timber bowling lane and may also be made of plastic. Its surface rises from the bowling position toward the first pin. The drawing shows the lane layout and its overall measurements.

fichas.title: Tapered (Scissor) Bowling Lane
fichas.summary: The tapered, or scissor, lane may be timber or plastic. It widens after 9.5 m to a stated width at the centre of the pins. The drawing shows the lane layout and indicates that the surface rises evenly between labeled points.
uses: Roll a ball toward the pins on a widening lane
